slice: daedalus/*.py basenames m-z plus __init__.py (root modules, second half) — 29 files
summary: This half of the root package holds the live offload cascade (offload -> provider_router -> sensitivity -> verifier -> preservation) and the Gate-0 contract/primitive layer (schemas, storage, primary_tree). The cascade is genuinely wired and heavily tested; the Gate-0 contract layer is almost entirely unconsumed. Seven of the eight canonical contracts in daedalus/schemas.py (MissionContract, AttemptContract, EvidencePacket, CampaignContract, PolicyDecision, RuntimeManifest, AttemptReceipt) have zero production importers — only tests/test_kernel_contracts.py — so the effectful path and the canonical contract path do not meet. Around that core sit a set of honest islands (memstore, runbook, token_monitor, shift_ticker, skills, semantic_route) and two self-declared compatibility shims to daedalus.kairos (mission_control, orchestrate). Health overall: the safety mechanics are real and measured, the kernel wiring named by Gate 0 is not yet closed.

modules.purpose: Three disjoint gates — data egress (fail-closed), write confinement (NOT fail-closed by default), and change-risk classification.
issues: Widest fan-in in the slice (~28 production importers plus tools/audit_swarm.py:55) and the most-tested. The asymmetry it documents at sensitivity.py:1-20 is real and load-bearing: write_allow empty means UNCONFINED, so write confinement is only as strong as the project policy actually loaded — which is precisely why offload.py refuses live writes without a policy.
It is the de facto effect policy, but it is not the PolicyDecision contract (schemas.py:1125): decisions it makes are never emitted as canonical policy records.

docs.reason: Describes the tabbed VS Code Mission Control dashboard in the present tense as a shipping surface, but tests/test_ui_governance.py:331 asserts the underlying dashboardHtml template is UNREACHABLE and must be labelled so, and daedalus/mission_control.py is a shim nothing imports. The doc is the strongest remaining reason a reader would believe this surface is live.
The narrow format-only adoption decision that daedalus/skills.py implements and cites; it is the reason skills.py correctly refuses to become a second scheduler. Still accurate.

integration_gaps: GATE-0 CENTRAL GAP: daedalus/schemas.py defines the canonical Gate-0 contracts but 7 of 8 have zero production consumers — MissionContract (schemas.py:520), AttemptContract (:579), EvidencePacket (:769), CampaignContract (:1011), PolicyDecision (:1125), RuntimeManifest (:1184), AttemptReceipt (:1318) appear only in schemas.py and tests/test_kernel_contracts.py. Only PromotionReceipt reaches production (spine/promotion_approval.py:567). Gate 0's 'canonical Mission, Attempt, Evidence, Campaign, policy, and receipt schemas' exist as definitions, not as the spine.

The live effect path bypasses the effect boundary: daedalus/offload.py performs guarded local-model writes and contains no reference to daedalus.spine.effect_boundary or any canonical contract. Gate 0 requires a 'centralized start/guard path for every effectful runtime entrypoint'; offload carries its own local guards instead.

In daedalus/spine/effect_boundary.py the registry is 40x Wiring.INVENTORY_ONLY, 8x CENTRAL, 6x LOCAL_GUARDS, 4x UNGUARDED, 1x ABSENT. Registration is not routing — inventoried effectful entrypoints from this slice (cli.runbook:549, cli.selftest:550, cli.shift:551, cli.status:552, cli.token_monitor:566, cli.web_api:573, web.mutations_put:605) are named but not centrally guarded.

Routing produces no canonical record: router.py picks the role, provider_router.py picks the provider and the egress/write authority, sensitivity.py makes the actual allow/deny call — and none of them emit a PolicyDecision (schemas.py:1125). Invariant 8's decisions are made but not recorded in canonical form.
Verification produces no canonical evidence: verifier.py:23 validates against the legacy schemas.validate_report, so accept/escalate verdicts never become EvidenceItem/EvidencePacket records.

Candidate bytes from the offload cascade are never content-addressed: daedalus/storage.py's artifact store is reached only from spine/attempt.py:148 and kairos/worktree.py:87, not from offload.py. Invariant 2 holds on one path only.

The worktree fence is path-dependent: daedalus/primary_tree.py (device/inode identity, undeniable) is imported only by spine/attempt.py:128 and eval/correctness.py:117; offload's write confinement rests on the weaker, policy-dependent sensitivity.path_write_blocked.

Three parallel append-only hash-chained ledgers of the same shape: daedalus/memstore.py (no consumers), daedalus/council/bus.py (which states at bus.py:13 that it deliberately reimplements memstore rather than importing it), and daedalus/spine/ledger.py. Invariant 1 asks for one event spine.

runtime_registry.py has a declared adapter into RuntimeManifest (schemas.py:1277) but, since RuntimeManifest has no production consumer, no Runtime Manifest is ever produced at runtime — the Gate-0 'vendor-neutral Agent Contract / Runtime Manifest' deliverable stops at the type.
notable: STALE MODULE DOCSTRING / stale package copy: build/lib/daedalus/ contains a 68-file copy of the whole package from an old `pip install .` run. build/lib/daedalus/schemas.py is 3167 bytes dated Jul 5 (the pre-Gate-0 legacy-only version) against the live 71525-byte file — a full second copy of every module in this slice, importable if the path is ever wrong, and a false hit for every future grep.

STALE DOCSTRING: daedalus/semantic_route.py:261-263 preserves a measurement ('MEASURED never run in production: 0 of 5 live probes') that describes the module BEFORE the cold-timeout fix at :270 was applied. As written a reader cannot tell whether the latent route runs today; the negative evidence is correctly retained but is not dated or superseded by a post-fix probe.

STALE DOCSTRING: daedalus/status.py's opening tells the story of a redesign and points readers to daedalus.health as 'the answer', while the module still ships the six counters it argues against — accurate but written as a changelog, so a reader learns the history before learning what the module does.
STALE DOCSTRING: daedalus/tools/inventory.py:3 still says skills.py 'had no consumer but its own tests' — true when written, now false, since inventory.py itself is that consumer (inventory.py:26).

Honest self-reporting is a real strength of this slice: preservation.py explicitly refuses to be called a gate ('A gate people believe is stronger than it is, is worse than no gate'), sensitivity.py names its own non-fail-closed default for write confinement, progress.py enumerates three past incidents where a claim was reported as a measurement, and shift.py/shift_hook.py document the exact 2026-07-30 clock failure they close. These are the docstrings to preserve verbatim in any consolidation.

tests/test_mapping_drift.py:316-333 encodes the island count as a PROPERTY rather than a magic number and names decompose.py, drafts.py and mission_control.py as real shims nothing reaches — the repo already measures its own dead weight, which makes the shims in this slice deletable with mechanical confidence.

docs/research/census/reviews/rv19.md:7 independently flags shift_hook.py, arch_hook.py and shift_ticker.py as files with CLAIMS but no symbols in the census, i.e. their guarantees are unverifiable — matching the island verdicts here.

daedalus/schemas.py is a single 71KB file holding two contract GENERATIONS (canonical at 217-1789, legacy AgentTask/AgentReport/RunState at 1791-1880). The package's public API (daedalus/__init__.py:4) exports only the legacy half. Splitting these would make the adoption gap visible instead of implicit.

daedalus/projects.py resolves repo_root for 17 importers and is effectively the workspace/write-root authority, yet has no docstring and no stated contract (the file opens directly with imports at line 1).
